content.comment_body: Hello, What is the best way to achieve accurate time synchronization between a PC and the [product_name] device? The current clock sync feature only allows setting minutes, not seconds. Even if seconds could be adjusted, manually entering the time can never be completely precise. Is there a method to synchronize with an NTP server or directly use PC timing without manual input? Ideally, I want a single action to use the PC time and update the [product_name]. The reason is that the datalog needs to match another system's logs, but at the moment, they are offset by 30 seconds to a minute. The other system uses NTP or PC timing, but I can't seem to do that for [product_name].

From what I know, [product_name] only synchronizes hours and minutes, with seconds always set to 0. Automatic syncing for the [product_name] [article_no] works only with the [product_name] module CMR, but even then, only hours and minutes are synchronized.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that [product_name] devices have a limitation where time synchronization can only be set to hours and minutes, not seconds. This causes discrepancies of up to a minute when aligning logs with other systems that use NTP or PC timing. The absence of direct or automated syncing with a PC or NTP server presents challenges for use cases needing precise timestamping.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to support precise time synchronization down to the second and the ability to sync automatically with a PC or NTP server, preferably with a simple sync operation.
